outcome: The authoring/compiler contract is now a stable language skeleton while implemented capabilities own their concrete authoring surfaces
owner_impact: The Virtual Lab wall is not softened. Programs that were valid before remain valid, unsupported observations remain blocked, host filesystem/network access remains forbidden, and controller RNG remains unavailable because no implemented controller-RNG capability exists. Research AI now sees concrete authoring surfaces on implemented capability entries instead of an exhaustive capability inventory embedded inside the authoring contract.

next.text: Next is #374, which makes new requests born as structured candidate capabilities or structured candidate contract deltas and reuses existing candidates rather than translating request prose later.

technical_evidence: The stable authoring contract is vlab.authoring/0.9; MCP server/interface are 3.11.0 / 15.
The 11 implemented canonical capabilities are unchanged. Their build-time bindings now carry typed authoring surfaces and are mirrored byte-identically between browser and edge validation.
Controller observation fields, neighbour fields, private state and Motion are resolved from implemented capability bindings rather than hard-coded into the stable Controller contract.
Controller rng.uniform remains rejected as semantic_capability because no implemented controller RNG surface exists; filesystem/network remain the explicit controller security roots.
The authoring contract no longer embeds canonical_capability_bindings or the current observation/action inventory. Neutral MCP discovery joins authoring_surfaces onto canonical capability entries.
No capability-request lifecycle, Professor workflow, scientific capability implementation, simulator runtime, CI/CD, retry, timeout, scheduling or development-workflow rule is changed.
